title: Finiteness descends to a stage of an algebraic-space inverse system
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Local finite presentation and local finite type are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(B_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces with affine transitions and limit $B$, and choose $i_0\in I$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism over $B_{i_0}$ with $X_0,Y_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $i\geq i_0$ put $X_i=X_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$ and let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$; let $f:X\to Y$ be its base change to $B$. A finite morphism is representable by schemes and finite on every scheme test [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. If $f_0$ is locally of finite type and $f$ is finite, then there is $j\geq i_0$ such that $f_i$ is finite for every $i\geq j$.

source.place: Tag 084Z (lemma-descend-finite) in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property); persistence under later base change.

proof.text: Restrict to the directed tail $i\geq i_0$. Choose an affine scheme $V_0$ and a representable surjective etale map $V_0\to Y_0$. Put $V_i=V_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$ and $W_0=X_0\times_{Y_0}V_0$, $W_i=W_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$. Associativity of sheaf fibre products identifies $V_i=Y_i\times_{Y_0}V_0$ and $W_i=X_i\times_{Y_i}V_i$; write $g_i:W_i\to V_i$. Every $V_i\to Y_i$ is representable surjective etale by base change. The affine-scheme qcqs lemma gives $V_0$ qcqs, and the qcqs fibre-product lemma, applied to $X_0,V_0,Y_0$, gives $W_0$ qcqs.

source.place: Tag 084Z (lemma-descend-finite), choice of affine etale chart; Tags 03H6 and 073B

proof.text: The affine transitions $B_i\to B_{i_0}$ give affine maps $V_i\to V_0$ and $W_i\to W_0$, as well as affine transition maps between the $V_i$ and between the $W_i$. Consequently $V_i$ is an affine scheme and $W_i$ is qcqs, by affine locality and permanence. Since $X_0$ is quasi-compact and $Y_0$ is quasi-separated, $f_0$ is quasi-compact. Together with its assumed local finite type this makes $f_0$ finite type. Finite type is preserved by arbitrary algebraic-space base change, so each $g_i$ is finite type. Once $W_i$ is a scheme, the identity scheme charts in the definition of local finite type give local finite type of the scheme morphism $g_i$.

source.place: Tag 084Z, hypotheses for the scheme descent step; Tags 03XH and 073B

proof.text: Set $V=V_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B$ and $W=W_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B$. The base-change formula for algebraic-space limits gives $V=\varprojlim V_i$ and $W=\varprojlim W_i$. The projection $B\to B_{i_0}$ is affine, so $V$ is an affine scheme. Fibre-product associativity identifies $W=X\times_Y V$, and $g:W\to V$ with the base change of $f$. Thus $g$ is a finite morphism of schemes by the assumed finiteness of $f$ on scheme tests. In particular $g$ is affine, so $W$ is affine. Apply eventual affineness to the qcqs system $(W_i)$ with affine transitions: there is $k\geq i_0$ such that $W_k$ is an affine scheme. All $W_i$ for $i\geq k$ are then affine schemes as well.

source.place: Tag 084Z, reduction to an affine stage by Tags 07SF and 07SQ

proof.text: Reindex at $k$ and regard $(V_i)_{i\geq k}$ as an inverse system of affine schemes with limit $V$. This is also a scheme limit: its algebraic-space universal property restricts to scheme tests. The cartesian identities give $W_i=W_k\times_{V_k}V_i$ and $W=W_k\times_{V_k}V$. Explicitly, both sides of the first identity classify a point of $X_0$, a point of $V_0$, and a point of $B_i$ with the prescribed equal images in $Y_0$ and $B_{i_0}$; the second identity is the same statement with $B$. Apply scheme finiteness descent to the $V_k$-morphism $g_k:W_k\to V_k$. Its initial base $V_k$, source $W_k$ and target $V_k$ are affine and hence qcqs, its scheme morphism is locally of finite type by step 2, the transition maps of the bases $V_i$ are affine, and its limit morphism is the finite map $g$. Therefore $g_j$ is finite for some $j\geq k$.

The map $V_j\to Y_j$ is a representable surjective etale scheme chart, and its pullback of $f_j$ is the finite scheme morphism $g_j$. The etale target criterion for finiteness therefore makes $f_j$ representable and finite. For every $i\geq j$, fibre-product associativity identifies $f_i$ with the base change of $f_j$ along $Y_i\to Y_j$. Stability of finite morphisms under arbitrary algebraic-space base change gives finiteness of every $f_i$, as required.
